title: Yuki Bhambri Eyes Deeper US Open Run After Last Year's Breakthrough Doubles Semifinal
excerpt: The Indian tennis star reunites with New Zealand's Michael Venus at Flushing Meadows, calling it a 'mental switch' after reaching the 2025 semifinals.
body:
• Yuki Bhambri and Michael Venus open their 2026 US Open men's doubles campaign against Ryan Seggerman and Patrik Trhac, with their round-one match scheduled for September 5.
  • The pair reached the semifinals at the 2025 US Open — the best Grand Slam doubles result of Bhambri's career — before falling to Joe Salisbury and Neal Skupski in three sets.
  • Bhambri, 34, describes the return as a "mental switch," saying the experience of being one match from the final has changed his mindset heading into the tournament.
  • The Delhi-born player highlighted the support from Indian fans at Flushing Meadows as part of what makes the US Open special for him.

Indian tennis player Yuki Bhambri returned to Flushing Meadows for the 2026 US Open with unfinished business. Reuniting with New Zealand's Michael Venus for the men's doubles, the 34-year-old is channeling last year's breakthrough semifinal run into what he hopes will be an even deeper campaign at the final Grand Slam of the season.

A Breakthrough to Build On

At the 2025 US Open, Bhambri and Venus — seeded 14th — put together the best Grand Slam doubles result of Bhambri's career. The pair stunned fourth-seeded Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz in the third round, then knocked out 11th seeds Rajeev Ram and Nikola Mektic 6-3, 6-7, 6-3 in the quarterfinals. Their run ended in the semifinals against Joe Salisbury and Neal Skupski, falling 6-7(2), 7-6(5), 6-4 in a match that lasted nearly three hours.

For a player who had never previously advanced past the third round of any Grand Slam in any category, the semifinal represented a career milestone. But Bhambri insists it has also reshaped his mental approach.

"I think it's a bit of a mental switch, having made a deep run and being quite close to making the final last year. Obviously, last year was spectacular for me and a bit of a breakthrough moment."

— Yuki Bhambri, in an interview with JioStar

New York and the Indian Crowd

Bhambri, who grew up in Delhi, has developed a particular affinity with New York and the energy that surrounds the US Open. He pointed to the size of the Indian contingent in the crowds at Flushing Meadows as a factor that elevates the experience.

"I love New York, it's one of my favourite cities," Bhambri told JioStar. "It's the best place in the world to play tennis. Coming from a big city like Delhi and seeing all the people around, as well as getting all the support, is great. Obviously, it's a great crowd over here, with a lot of Indians coming out and supporting. It's absolutely electric."

The former junior world No. 1 said he and Venus plan to take the tournament match by match while believing they can produce another deep run.

First-Round Draw

Bhambri and Venus opened their 2026 campaign against Ryan Seggerman and Patrik Trhac in the first round, with the match scheduled for September 5 at 8:30 PM. Their path through the draw will determine whether the 2025 semifinal was a one-off breakthrough or the beginning of a sustained Grand Slam doubles presence for one of India's most experienced players on the ATP tour.
